top_strength: Erik de-escalated a stressed, budget-strapped customer by working collaboratively through two concrete pricing options (6hr/$1,387 vs 5hr/$1,085) while validating his situation ('I get it, dude, they're head hunting these days'), turning an anxious cost complaint into an appreciative close.
coaching_note: This was a post-booking renegotiation call, not a fresh sales pitch, so several Section 3/7 differentiators (No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, no-hidden-fees, deposit language) are legitimately N/A since they were already delivered at original booking — don't read this score as a clean pitch-quality mastery check either way. That said, the Save Your Ass miss (0/10) is a real gap, not an artifact of call type: the customer was actively trying to shrink cost/time, which is exactly the moment to proactively pitch consolidation and carload self-prep tips instead of only cutting contracted hours.
phone_presence_notes: Erik used consistent empathetic language ('no worries at all,' 'I get it, dude'), shared a relatable personal anecdote about apartment costs, and the customer's tone visibly warmed from anxious to appreciative by the end of the call.
